title: A single tensor-kernel witness for a map into a Mittag-Leffler module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $P$ a finitely presented $R$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], $M$ an $R$-module that is Mittag-Leffler in the tensor-product sense [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], and $f:P\to M$ an $R$-linear map. Tensor products and induced maps are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There exist an $R$-module $T$, whose underlying collection is a set, and $z\in P\otimes_RT$ with $(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)=0$ such that, for every finitely presented $R$-module $Q$ and every $x\in\ker(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)$, there is an $R$-linear map $q:T\to Q$ satisfying $(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes q)(z)=x$. No flatness hypothesis is imposed on $P$, $M$ or $Q$.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof of (2) implies (1): finite-presentation representatives, product of all kernel pairs, and the first commutative square; tensor-product input Tag 059K (proposition-fp-tensor).

proof.text: For each pair $m,n\in\mathbf N$ and each $n\times m$ matrix $a$ over $R$, form $Q_a=R^n/\operatorname{im}(a:R^m\to R^n)$. These matrix codes form a set $B$, and the definition of finite presentation gives an $R$-linear isomorphism $e:Q_a\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ for every finitely presented $Q$: a presentation surjection $R^n\to Q$ sends a coset to the image of any representative; exactness makes this well-defined and bijective. Put $A=\{(a,y):a\in B,\ y\in P\otimes_RQ_a,\ (f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_a})(y)=0\}$. Each tensor product is a set by its quotient construction, so $A$ is a set. For $\alpha=(a,y)$ write $Q_\alpha=Q_a$ and $y_\alpha=y$, and set $T=\prod_{\alpha\in A}Q_\alpha$, with componentwise module operations. Its underlying collection is a set.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof of (2) implies (1), the set B, pairs A and first commutative square; Tag 059K (proposition-fp-tensor), implication (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-tensor-products] to the finitely presented module $P$ and the set-indexed family $(Q_\alpha)$. The tuple $(y_\alpha)_\alpha$ has a preimage $z\in P\otimes_RT$ under the bijective comparison map. Thus $(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes\pi_\alpha)(z)=y_\alpha$ for every coordinate projection $\pi_\alpha:T\to Q_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof of (2) implies (1), the set B, pairs A and first commutative square; Tag 059K (proposition-fp-tensor), implication (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Put $w=(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)$. The $\alpha$-coordinate of $\theta_{M,(Q_\alpha)}(w)$ equals $(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_\alpha})(y_\alpha)=0$. Indeed the identity $(\mathrm{id}_M\otimes\pi_\alpha)(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)=(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_\alpha})(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes\pi_\alpha)$ holds on $p\otimes t$, since both sides give $f(p)\otimes\pi_\alpha(t)$, and hence holds everywhere by generation by pure tensors. The Mittag-Leffler definition makes $\theta_{M,(Q_\alpha)}$ injective, so $w=0$.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof of (2) implies (1), the set B, pairs A and first commutative square; Tag 059K (proposition-fp-tensor), implication (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Given finitely presented $Q$ and $x\in\ker(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)$, choose $a\in B$ and $e:Q_a\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ as in step 1. Set $y=(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes e^{-1})(x)$. Checking on $p\otimes q$ gives $(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_a})(y)=(\mathrm{id}_M\otimes e^{-1})((f\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)(x))=0$. Hence $\alpha=(a,y)\in A$. Define $q=e\circ\pi_\alpha:T\to Q$. Then $(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes q)(z)=(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes e)(y)=x$: composition of induced maps is checked on pure tensors, and $e\circ e^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_Q$. This proves both required properties without any flatness assumption.
